adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — Unsubscribe mutates notification level on a plain GET (HTML and .json) with no CSRF token, so any ``, including one embedded in a forum post, silently steps down or mutes topics for every logged-in viewer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `unsubscribe` action that *changes state* (toggles `TopicUser.notification_level` and `tu.save!`) in `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, and wires it up via `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (also non-slug variant). Since it’s a GET endpoint, it will not require a CSRF token under typical Rails defaults, and it can be triggered by a cross-site request like an `` for any logged-in user whose cookies are sent, causing silent notification-level changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — The endpoint is not idempotent: each visit (reload, back/forward, session restore, browser prerender, double click) steps the level down again (watching/tracking -> regular -> muted), so a user who meant to drop to regular ends up muted without ever choosing that.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the GET endpoint changes state by toggling based on current `TopicUser.notification_level`: if `tu.notification_level > regular` it sets to `regular`, otherwise it sets to `muted`. That means a second visit/reload after dropping from watching/tracking to regular will flip the user again to muted (because the level is now `regular`), so the operation is not idempotent and repeated navigations can unintentionally mute the topic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:108 — The first click only lowers tracking/watching to regular, and regular still sends reply, mention and quote emails, so a user clicking "stop receiving notifications" from a reply email keeps getting the same emails.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code explicitly *does not* always stop notifications: it toggles the user’s `TopicUser.notification_level` between `:regular` and `:muted` (if current level is `> :regular` it sets it to `:regular`, else it sets to `:muted`). This means a first click from an email by a user currently watching/tracking the topic will only downgrade them to `regular`, not fully mute/stop topic notifications. That conflicts with the added email copy (`server.en.yml`: “To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here”) and the client copy (`client.en.yml`: “You will stop receiving notifications for …”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/client.en.yml:985 — The page always says "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>" even when the server only lowered the level to regular, so the user is told something false.

adjudication.rationale: The unsubscribe page always renders the client i18n string `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` (template `topic/unsubscribe.hbs` uses `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`), but the server action `TopicsController#unsubscribe` intentionally toggles notification level: if the user was above `:regular` (e.g., tracking/watching), it lowers to `:regular`; otherwise it sets to `:muted`. From the diff alone, you cannot verify that changing to `:regular` means the user will still receive topic notifications in a way that makes the copy "You will stop receiving notifications..." false—`regular` may be the intended “stop topic notifications” state. The finding asserts incorrect behavior semantics not established by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by` can return nil (e.g., a different logged-in user opens a forwarded link, or the user has no topic_users row), and `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError, a 500.

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — Writing the level directly with `tu.save!` skips `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_reason_id` stays nil and `update_last_read` later auto-promotes the muted/regular topic back to tracking; it also skips the MessageBus publish and `notifications_changed_at`.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the PR updates `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly. The diff shows `TopicUser.change` is the place that performs side effects when `notification_level` changes (notably `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)`). By bypassing `TopicUser.change`, this new unsubscribe flow will not emit the notification-level change event and likely misses any other change-related bookkeeping handled there. The finding’s additional claims about `notification_reason_id` and `update_last_read` auto-promoting aren’t verifiable from this diff, but the skipped side effects are.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6 — The Ember route only loads the topic view and never calls the server unsubscribe endpoint, so client-side navigation to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (e.g., an in-app link) shows the "you will stop receiving notifications" confirmation without changing anything.

adjudication.rationale: The new Ember route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` only loads the topic view via `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` and then renders the unsubscribe UI, but it never performs a request to the new Rails endpoint `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (wired in `config/routes.rb` as `t/:.../unsubscribe`) that actually toggles `TopicUser.notification_level`. Therefore, a client-side transition to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` within the SPA can show the confirmation text/template (`templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`) without changing notification state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic.rb:719 — The per-topic link carries no user token (unlike the key-based digest unsubscribe), so it acts on whoever is logged in in that browser, and logged-out clicks (the common case from mail clients on another device) hit ensure_logged_in instead of unsubscribing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a per-topic unsubscribe link in emails via `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and `Topic#unsubscribe_url` returns a generic URL (`"#{url}/unsubscribe"`) with no user-specific token. The new controller action `TopicsController#unsubscribe` applies changes to `TopicUser` using `current_user` (`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`) and has no handling for a nil `current_user`, so the link inherently requires an authenticated session and will act on whichever user is currently logged in in that browser. This matches the finding: logged-out clicks won’t unsubscribe (likely redirected/blocked) and logged-in-as-someone-else could unsubscribe the wrong account.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:171 — The spec adds `unsubscribe_url` only so I18n does not raise, but never asserts the per-topic link is in the body, and no controller spec covers the level transitions, the nil TopicUser case or the login requirement, so the tests pass while the feature is broken.

adjudication.rationale: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action assumes a logged-in user and an existing `TopicUser` row: it calls `current_user.id` and then `tu.notification_level` without guarding against `current_user == nil` or `tu == nil` (`tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)`). Either case will raise at runtime, so the feature can break even though the updated email spec only supplies `unsubscribe_url` and doesn’t assert the per-topic link rendering. These are concrete correctness issues visible in the diff, not just a generic “add more tests” request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 — unsubscribe_link` now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, so any current or future caller (plugin or other mailer) that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` gets I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and the whole email fails to build.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` so `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, the unsubscribe HTML is always built via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but `template_args` has no default `unsubscribe_url` (only `site_name`, `base_url`, `user_preferences_url`, plus caller-provided opts). Therefore, any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also providing `unsubscribe_url` will trigger an `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at email build time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:500 — Explicit `render :show` in shared perform_show_response renders the layout before `show` calls canonical_url (line 87), so topic pages lose their computed canonical link (falls back to request URL).

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `perform_show_response` now doing `render :show` for `format.html` and adds a new `unsubscribe` action that calls `perform_show_response`. The diff does not show any `canonical_url` call in `show` (or its relative ordering), nor any evidence that the canonical link computation depends on implicit rendering. From the diff alone, the claim that topic pages “lose their computed canonical link” cannot be verified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — Unsubscribe writes via `tu.save!` instead of TopicUser.change, skipping the MessageBus notification_level_change publish and notifications_reason_id/changed_at, so open clients go stale and update_last_read auto-tracking (reason_id null) can flip the topic back to tracking.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows `tu.notification_level = ...` followed by `tu.save!` (new code in `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`). The diff also shows `TopicUser.change` publishes a MessageBus `notification_level_change` event when `attrs[:notification_level]` is set (`app/models/topic_user.rb`), which `save!` bypasses. So this action will not emit the real-time update to open clients and will skip any other side effects encapsulated in `TopicUser.change` (the finding’s core claim is verifiable from the diff, though the specific `notification_reason_id/changed_at` and auto-tracking flip details aren’t shown here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — State-changing GET route is a non-idempotent toggle (watching/tracking->regular->muted), so reloads, link prefetchers, or cross-site GETs (CSRF via img src) silently escalate to muted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that is reachable via GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). That action mutates server state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` (downgrades >regular to regular, otherwise sets muted) and `tu.save!`. Because it’s a state-changing GET (and `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]` allows non-XHR), it is vulnerable to accidental triggering (reload/prefetch) and cross-site GET/CSRF-style triggering (e.g., ``), causing silent notification state changes to muted/regular as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by` can return nil (logged-in user with no topic_users row for that topic), and `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError, so the public endpoint returns 500 instead of a 4xx.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6 — Ember topicUnsubscribe route only loads the topic view JSON and never calls the server unsubscribe endpoint, so client-side navigation to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe shows the "you will stop receiving notifications" copy while nothing changes.

adjudication.rationale: In the new Ember route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the `model(params)` hook only calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` (i.e., loads the normal topic view JSON) and never performs a request to the new Rails unsubscribe endpoint (`TopicsController#unsubscribe`, routed at `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe`). Therefore, if the user reaches `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` via client-side routing (no full-page reload), the route will render the unsubscribe template but will not trigger the server-side toggle of `TopicUser.notification_level` implemented in `TopicsController#unsubscribe`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 — Shared `unsubscribe_link` i18n string now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, so any MessageBuilder caller with add_unsubscribe_link but no unsubscribe_url raises MissingInterpolationArgument (the spec had to be patched), and the topic-specific wording is forced onto every such email.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the shared server i18n key `unsubscribe_link` to include a new interpolation `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml). `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true (lib/email/message_builder.rb) but does not supply a default `unsubscribe_url`, so any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will raise `MissingInterpolationArgument`. The spec was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, indicating this breakage is real for that call pattern, and the topic-specific text is now baked into the global `unsubscribe_link` string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/client.en.yml:985 — Confirmation copy says notifications stop entirely, but the server only drops watching/tracking to regular (mentions and replies still notify), so the UI and server semantics disagree.

adjudication.rationale: The new client copy `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications: "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}."` implies notifications will cease after visiting the unsubscribe link. However, the new server action `TopicsController#unsubscribe` does not always stop notifications: it changes `TopicUser.notification_level` from watching/tracking/etc. down to `:regular` when `tu.notification_level > :regular`, only setting to `:muted` otherwise. So for users currently watching/tracking, the server leaves them at `regular` (not “no notifications”), making the confirmation text inaccurate relative to the behavior shown in the diff.
